data.narrative:
Project Omega, a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Stafford Sheehan, has raised $12M to date and lacks a current independent valuation. The nuclear energy sector comp universe comprises 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, X-Energy, and Oklo, though the seed-stage peer set is sparse.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow comparables—only 1 same-stage and 1 adjacent-stage peer exist in the nuclear sector, below the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints required for reliable triangulation. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $12M total raised proxy, reflecting typical step-up multiples from seed to next-stage funding. This method yields an implied valuation of $30M.

The triangulated range spans $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median of $30M. The narrow range reflects reliance on a single applicable method rather than cross-validation across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for the nuclear subsector, the absence of recent comparable seed rounds, and execution risk inherent to early-stage frontier technology. A more robust valuation would require either additional same-stage nuclear peers or broader sector metrics as secondary anchors.
